content: 1. Exercise caution when transitioning patients from long-acting therapies that have immune-modulating effects, as these can influence subsequent treatments. 2. Golimumab reduces the efficacy of the Haemophilus influenzae type b vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored in such cases. 3. Vaccination should be avoided during chemotherapy or radiation therapy whenever possible, as the antibody response may be suboptimal. Patients vaccinated within 14 days before starting or during immunosuppressive therapy should be revaccinated approximately three months after discontinuation of therapy, provided immune competence has been restored. 4. Hydroxyurea and golimumab may increase the risk of immunosuppression when used together. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 5. Golimumab diminishes the effects of the influenza virus vaccine (quadrivalent, recombinant) through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Immune response to vaccines may be reduced in immunocompromised individuals. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Golimumab and isavuconazonium sulfate both reduce immunosuppressive effects, potentially increasing the risk of infection. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 7. Golimumab increases immunosuppressive effects, while maitake decreases them, leading to unclear interaction outcomes. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Golimumab reduces the efficacy of the meningococcal group B vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Individuals with altered immune competence may exhibit reduced immune responses to the vaccine. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Golimumab and mercaptopurine both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Caution and monitoring are required. 10. Ofatumumab SC and golimumab each amplify the immunosuppressive effects of the other, raising the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. When co-administering immunosuppressive therapies, consider the potential for additive immune system effects. When switching from therapies with immune effects, account for the duration and mechanism of action of these therapies when initiating ofatumumab SC. 12. Golimumab and olaparib exhibit pharmacodynamic synergism, necessitating caution and monitoring. 13. Co-administration of golimumab with other myelosuppressive anticancer agents, including DNA-damaging agents, may intensify and prolong myelosuppressive toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Golimumab reduces the efficacy of the inactivated poliovirus vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 15. Rozanolixizumab decreases the level or effect of golimumab through receptor binding competition. Co-administration with medications that bind to the human neonatal Fc receptor may lower systemic exposures and effectiveness of such medications. Monitor closely for reduced effectiveness, and consider alternative therapies if long-term use is essential. 16. Golimumab reduces the efficacy of sipuleucel-T due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 17. Trastuzumab and golimumab increase each other's toxicity through immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Neutropenia or febrile neutropenia incidence increases when trastuzumab is co-administered with myelosuppressive chemotherapy. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Ublituximab and golimumab both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 19. Golimumab reduces the efficacy of the recombinant zoster vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Immunosuppressive therapies may reduce the effectiveness of the recombinant zoster vaccine. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Patients receiving immunosuppressives alongside golimumab may face a higher risk of developing infections. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Golimumab and adalimumab both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 22. Golimumab and alefacept both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 23. Golimumab and anakinra both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. Golimumab reduces the efficacy of the anthrax vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Immunosuppressants also increase the risk of infection with concomitant live vaccines. 25. Golimumab and antithymocyte globulin (equine or rabbit) both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 26. Golimumab increases immunosuppressive effects, while astragalus decreases them, leading to unclear interaction outcomes. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Golimumab and axicabtagene ciloleucel each amplify the immunosuppressive effects of the other, raising the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 28. Golimumab and azathioprine both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 29. Golimumab and baricitinib both increase each other's toxicity through immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Baricitinib is not recommended in combination with other JAK inhibitors, biologic DMARDs, or potent immunosuppressives. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 30. Golimumab and basiliximab both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 31. Golimumab reduces the efficacy of the BCG vaccine (live) due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Immunosuppressants also increase the risk of infection with concomitant live vaccines. 32. Golimumab and belatacept both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Golimumab and brexucabtagene autoleucel each amplify the immunosuppressive effects of the other, raising the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 34. Golimumab and canakinumab both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 35. Golimumab and certolizumab pegol both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 36. Golimumab and ciltacabtagene autoleucel each amplify the immunosuppressive effects of the other, raising the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 37. Golimumab and cyclosporine both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 38. Golimumab reduces the efficacy of the dengue vaccine due to immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Immunosuppressive therapies may reduce the immune response to the dengue vaccine. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Golimumab and denosumab require caution in patients on concomitant immunosuppressants or with impaired immune systems due to an increased risk of serious infections. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Golimumab reduces the efficacy of diphtheria and tetanus toxoids due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Immunosuppressants also increase the risk of infection with concomitant live vaccines. 41. Golimumab reduces the efficacy of diphtheria, tetanus toxoids, and acellular pertussis vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Immunosuppressants also increase the risk of infection with concomitant live vaccines. 42. Golimumab reduces the efficacy of diphtheria, tetanus toxoids, acellular pertussis, and inactivated poliovirus vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Immunosuppressants also increase the risk of infection with concomitant live vaccines. 43. Golimumab increases immunosuppressive effects, while echinacea decreases them, leading to unclear interaction outcomes. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Efgartigimod alfa decreases the level or effect of golimumab through receptor binding competition. Co-administration with medications that bind to the human neonatal Fc receptor may lower systemic exposures and effectiveness of such medications. Monitor closely for reduced effectiveness, and consider alternative therapies if long-term use is essential. 45. Efgartigimod/hyaluronidase decreases the level or effect of golimumab through receptor binding competition. Co-administration with medications that bind to the human neonatal Fc receptor may lower systemic exposures and effectiveness of such medications. Monitor closely for reduced effectiveness, and consider alternative therapies if long-term use is essential. 46. Golimumab and etanercept both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 47. Golimumab and everolimus both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 48. Golimumab increases the effects of fingolimod through immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 49. Golimumab and glatiramer both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 50. Golimumab reduces the efficacy of the hepatitis A vaccine (inactivated) due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Immunosuppressants also increase the risk of infection with concomitant live vaccines. 51. Golimumab reduces the efficacy of the hepatitis A/B vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Immunosuppressants also increase the risk of infection with concomitant live vaccines. 52. Golimumab reduces the efficacy of the hepatitis A/typhoid vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Immunosuppressants also increase the risk of infection with concomitant live vaccines. 53. Golimumab reduces the efficacy of the hepatitis B vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Immunosuppressants also increase the risk of infection with concomitant live vaccines. 54. Golimumab reduces the efficacy of the human papillomavirus vaccine (nonavalent) due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Immunosuppressive therapies may reduce immune responses to vaccines. 55. Golimumab and hydroxychloroquine sulfate both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 56. Golimumab and idecabtagene vicleucel each amplify the immunosuppressive effects of the other, raising the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 57. Golimumab and infliximab both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 58. Golimumab reduces the efficacy of the influenza virus vaccine (quadrivalent) due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Immunosuppressants also increase the risk of infection with concomitant live vaccines. 59. Golimumab reduces the efficacy of the influenza virus vaccine (quadrivalent, adjuvanted) due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Immunosuppressive drugs may reduce the immune response to the influenza vaccine. 60. Golimumab reduces the efficacy of the influenza virus vaccine (quadrivalent, cell-cultured) due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Immunosuppressants also increase the risk of infection with concomitant live vaccines. 61. Golimumab reduces the efficacy of the influenza virus vaccine (quadrivalent, intranasal) due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Immunosuppressants also increase the risk of infection with concomitant live vaccines. 62. Golimumab reduces the efficacy of the influenza virus vaccine (quadrivalent, recombinant) due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Immune response to vaccines may be reduced in immunocompromised individuals. 63. Golimumab reduces the efficacy of the influenza virus vaccine (trivalent) due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Immunosuppressants also increase the risk of infection with concomitant live vaccines.
